findings.title: Delete-cache mutation never refreshes connectedCalendars data
findings.body: The deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional external onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same file (onSettled invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars), it never invalidates that query, and SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper's own query is not refetched by the external onChanged callback. After a successful deletion the dropdown therefore keeps showing the old cacheUpdatedAt timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until a manual reload, making it look like the deletion did nothing.

findings.title: Cache status ignores cache expiry
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, whereas getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. Credentials whose only cache entries are expired (up to a month old, no longer served) will still be reported as having cache, so the UI displays a 'Last updated' status and offers deletion for data that is already unusable, and the timestamp does not reflect any live cache.

findings.title: Pre-existing cache rows get migration time as updatedAt
findings.body: Adding updatedAt as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() stamps every legacy CalendarCache row with the migration/deployment time rather than its actual last-write time. Immediately after deploy, the new UI will present that deployment timestamp as 'Cache last updated' for all existing credentials, even for cache entries written weeks earlier, giving users a misleading freshness signal until each row happens to be rewritten.

findings.title: Handler bypasses the calendar-cache repository abstraction and always queries
findings.body: The handler directly instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository on every connectedCalendars call, instead of going through the CalendarCache/calendar-cache-disabled path that CalendarCacheRepositoryMock exists for. This adds a groupBy query to every connected-calendars load (including users with no Google credentials and orgs with calendar-cache disabled, where the mock would return []) and surfaces cache status/deletion for stale rows even when the cache feature is off.

findings.title: Committed dev script only works on macOS and writes outside the repo
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux treats '' as an input file and fails, so the script cannot update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL on Linux. Additionally ENV_FILE is hardcoded to ../.env relative to the caller's working directory, so running it from the repo root writes the tunnel URL to a .env outside the repository instead of the repo's .env. This unrelated local-testing script should not be merged in this form.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned npx tsx which is not a declared dependency
findings.body: tsx is not listed in apps/web (or root) dependencies, so `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` will download an unpinned package from the registry on first run. That breaks offline/air-gapped dev environments, is a supply-chain risk, and can silently change behavior as tsx releases change; tsx should be added as a pinned devDependency or the previously available ts-node kept.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US regardless of user locale
findings.body: The 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) even though the surrounding UI is localized via useLocale. Non-English users will see US-style dates (e.g. 7/15/25) inside otherwise translated text; the format should use the current user's locale.
